name: Electrical Assisted Bicycle
description: A vehicle with two or three wheels, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts, in one of three classes: Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph, Class 2 throttle to 20 mph, and Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: Class 1 and Class 3 assist only while the rider pedals, cutting out at 20 and 28 mph; Class 2 may assist without pedaling, to 20 mph (Colorado Revised Statutes §42-1-102(28.5))
Class 1 and 3 need a cutoff that can't be bypassed, stopping the motor when the rider stops pedaling; a Class 2 motor stops when the brakes are applied (Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221)

A vehicle modified out of every class, or built to be easily switched out of one by a button, setting or app, is not an electrical assisted bicycle (Colorado Revised Statutes §42-1-102(28.5), as amended by HB 25-1197)
A multiple-mode e-bike that can switch between classes must meet the rules of each class it can run as (Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221, as amended by HB 25-1197)
A multiple-mode e-bike's label must name each class it can run as (Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221, as amended by HB 25-1197)

Carries a permanent label, in Arial at least 9-point, stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage, and must not be modified to change its speed or motor engagement unless the label is replaced to match (Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221)

Sellers must disclose its wattage, top speed and class; selling a vehicle that isn't one as an e-bike without a written disclosure is a deceptive trade practice (Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221, as amended by HB 25-1197)
Its lithium-ion battery must be certified by an accredited lab to a UL 2849 or EN 15194 battery standard (Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221, as amended by HB 25-1197)
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512) (Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221)
Class 3 riders must be 16 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers (Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-1412)
Class 3 riders and passengers under 18 must wear a bicycle helmet meeting CPSC or ASTM standards, and a Class 3 must have a speedometer (Colorado Revised Statutes §§42-4-221, 42-4-1412)
Class 1 and Class 2 may ride bike and pedestrian paths where bicycles are allowed, but a local authority may ban them from its paths (Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-1412)
Class 3 is kept off bike and pedestrian paths unless the path is within a street or highway or the local authority allows it (Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-1412)
On a sidewalk it yields to pedestrians, and local ordinances or signs may ban it there (Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-1412)
In state parks, Class 1 and 2 may ride roads, bike lanes and trails open to bicycles; in state wildlife areas, e-bikes are limited to roads and camping or parking areas open to motor vehicles
Its rider has the same rights and duties as a bicyclist, and it is not a motor vehicle: no registration or driver's license (Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-1412)
